# Introduction

You are an experienced AI researcher. You have written code for your research experiment and now need to evaluate the output of the code execution. Analyze the execution output, determine if there were any bugs, and provide a summary of the findings.

# Research idea

{"Name": "shortcut_recovery_debt", "Title": "The Shortcut That Won\u2019t Let Go: Testing Recovery After Spurious-Cue Removal", "Short Hypothesis": "When a small MLP learns an easy but unreliable cue alongside a harder causal signal, removing that cue at evaluation will hurt more than training without it helps: under a small fixed training budget, the model will fail to recover the causal signal even when the cue is absent from later data. This isolates whether shortcut reliance creates a measurable recovery cost, rather than merely documenting performance under a shifted test distribution.", "Related Work": "Shortcut-learning and spurious-correlation research documents failures under distribution shift, while controlled synthetic studies commonly vary correlation strength, environments, or training procedures. This pilot asks a narrower intervention question: does exposure to a predictive shortcut impair learning the stable signal when the shortcut is subsequently unavailable? It uses a single synthetic task and matched data budgets, so it is a small mechanistic pilot, not a claim of broad novelty or generality. Semantic Scholar searches were rate-limited, so the literature check is incomplete and novelty remains unresolved.", "Abstract": "Deep learning systems can perform well by exploiting predictive cues that are easier to learn than the intended signal, then fail when those cues disappear. We propose a controlled pilot to measure a less-studied practical consequence: whether training with a shortcut makes later recovery of the stable signal harder. Generate two-dimensional examples with a binary label, a noisy stable feature correlated with the label, and a more accurate shortcut feature whose label correlation is high during training but absent at evaluation. Train the same small multilayer perceptron for five epochs in three conditions: stable feature only; stable feature plus shortcut; and stable feature plus shortcut with the shortcut masked for the final portion of training. Use identical sample budgets, fixed seeds, and separate training and validation data. Evaluate stable-signal accuracy and loss on a shortcut-free test set, alongside in-distribution accuracy and a linear probe or input ablation to assess reliance on each feature. The primary comparison is whether shortcut-exposed training yields lower shortcut-free accuracy than stable-only training, and whether late masking reduces that gap. With at most 2,048 training examples and 512 validation examples per condition, the experiment is inexpensive and directly tests the intervention. Results will be reported across several fixed seeds with uncertainty intervals. Any effect would motivate larger studies; this deliberately narrow synthetic pilot cannot establish that recovery debt generalizes to complex architectures or real-world deployment.", "Experiments": ["Generate independent train, validation, and test sets with NumPy/PyTorch. Each example has a stable scalar feature x_s = y + Gaussian noise and a shortcut scalar x_q = y times a sign variable plus Gaussian noise. In training and validation, the shortcut sign agrees with the label with probability 0.95; in the shortcut-free test set, it is independent of the label. Standardize using training statistics only.", "Compare three conditions with the same small MLP (2-16-16-1, ReLU, binary cross-entropy), optimizer, batch size, and five epochs: A) train on x_s only; B) train on x_s and x_q throughout; C) train on both initially, then set x_q to zero for the final two epochs. Keep each condition to at most 2,048 training examples and 512 validation examples; use independent held-out test examples. Run 10 fixed seeds, recording paired per-seed results.", "Primary metric: test accuracy with the shortcut uninformative. Secondary metrics: test binary cross-entropy, validation accuracy under the training correlation, and shortcut reliance measured by the accuracy change when x_q is zeroed on correlated validation inputs. Report mean differences and bootstrap confidence intervals across seeds; include learning curves and verify that the stable-only condition learns above chance."], "Risk Factors and Limitations": ["The result may depend strongly on feature noise, shortcut strength, initialization, and the chosen training schedule; a small grid over these parameters may be needed before drawing conclusions.", "Late masking changes the effective input distribution and may act as ordinary augmentation or regularization, so any benefit cannot by itself identify a unique mechanism.", "The synthetic two-feature setting is intentionally minimal. It cannot establish that recovery costs occur in larger networks, richer data, or deployed systems.", "Only five epochs and a small sample budget may fail to produce stable learning or a meaningful shortcut-reliance gap; report null or ambiguous results rather than tuning until an effect appears.", "Semantic Scholar retrieval was rate-limited during the literature check. Novelty should be verified against primary literature before making a strong originality claim."]}

# Implementation

```python
import os

working_dir = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), "working")
os.makedirs(working_dir, exist_ok=True)

import random
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset

device = torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
print(f"Using device: {device}")

experiment_data = {
    name: {
        "metrics": {"train": [], "val": []},
        "losses": {"train": [], "val": []},
        "predictions": [],
        "ground_truth": [],
        "epochs": [],
        "test_metrics": [],
        "test_losses": [],
        "shortcut_ablation_accuracy": [],
    }
    for name in ("stable_only", "shortcut_exposed", "late_masked")
}


def make_data(n, seed, split):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    y = rng.integers(0, 2, size=n).astype(np.float32)
    sign = 2 * y - 1
    stable = sign + rng.normal(0, 1.0, n)
    if split == "test":
        q_sign = rng.choice([-1.0, 1.0], size=n)
    else:
        agrees = rng.random(n) < 0.95
        q_sign = sign * np.where(agrees, 1.0, -1.0)
    shortcut = q_sign + rng.normal(0, 0.35, n)
    return np.column_stack([stable, shortcut]).astype(np.float32), y[:, None]


class MLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(2, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 1)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.net(x)


def evaluate(model, loader):
    model.eval()
    loss_fn = nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss(reduction="sum")
    total_loss, correct, count = 0.0, 0, 0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for xb, yb in loader:
            xb, yb = xb.to(device), yb.to(device)
            logits = model(xb)
            total_loss += loss_fn(logits, yb).item()
            correct += ((logits >= 0) == (yb >= 0.5)).sum().item()
            count += len(yb)
    return total_loss / count, correct / count


conditions = ("stable_only", "shortcut_exposed", "late_masked")
for seed in range(10):
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)

    x_train_raw, y_train_raw = make_data(2048, 1000 + seed, "train")
    x_val_raw, y_val_raw = make_data(512, 2000 + seed, "val")
    x_test_raw, y_test_raw = make_data(2048, 3000 + seed, "test")

    mean = x_train_raw.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)
    std = x_train_raw.std(axis=0, keepdims=True) + 1e-6
    x_train = (x_train_raw - mean) / std
    x_val = (x_val_raw - mean) / std
    x_test = (x_test_raw - mean) / std
    y_train = y_train_raw
    y_val = y_val_raw
    y_test = y_test_raw

    for condition in conditions:
        model = MLP().to(device)
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
        train_ds = TensorDataset(torch.from_numpy(x_train), torch.from_numpy(y_train))
        train_loader = DataLoader(train_ds, batch_size=128, shuffle=True)
        val_loader = DataLoader(
            TensorDataset(torch.from_numpy(x_val), torch.from_numpy(y_val)),
            batch_size=256,
            shuffle=False,
        )
        history = experiment_data[condition]
        for epoch in range(5):
            model.train()
            total_loss, correct, count = 0.0, 0, 0
            for xb, yb in train_loader:
                batch = {"x": xb, "y": yb}
                batch = {
                    k: v.to(device)
                    for k, v in batch.items()
                    if isinstance(v, torch.Tensor)
                }
                inputs = batch["x"].clone()
                if condition == "stable_only":
                    inputs[:, 1] = 0
                elif condition == "late_masked" and epoch >= 3:
                    inputs[:, 1] = 0
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                logits = model(inputs)
                loss = nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(
                    logits, batch["y"]
                )
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                total_loss += loss.item() * len(batch["y"])
                correct += ((logits.detach() >= 0) == (batch["y"] >= 0.5)).sum().item()
                count += len(batch["y"])

            train_loss, train_acc = total_loss / count, correct / count
            val_loss, val_acc = evaluate(model, val_loader)
            history["losses"]["train"].append(train_loss)
            history["losses"]["val"].append(val_loss)
            history["metrics"]["train"].append(train_acc)
            history["metrics"]["val"].append(val_acc)
            history["epochs"].append(epoch + 1)
            print(
                f"Seed {seed} | {condition} | Epoch {epoch + 1}: validation_loss = {val_loss:.4f}, validation_accuracy = {val_acc:.4f}"
            )

        test_x = torch.from_numpy(x_test).to(device)
        test_y = torch.from_numpy(y_test).to(device)
        model.eval()
        with torch.no_grad():
            test_logits = model(test_x)
            test_loss = nn.functional.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(
                test_logits, test_y
            ).item()
            test_pred = (test_logits >= 0).float()
            test_acc = (test_pred == test_y).float().mean().item()
            val_ablate = torch.from_numpy(x_val).to(device).clone()
            val_ablate[:, 1] = 0
            ablate_pred = (model(val_ablate) >= 0).float()
            ablate_acc = (
                (ablate_pred == torch.from_numpy(y_val).to(device))
                .float()
                .mean()
                .item()
            )

        history["test_metrics"].append(test_acc)
        history["test_losses"].append(test_loss)
        history["shortcut_ablation_accuracy"].append(ablate_acc)
        history["predictions"].append(test_pred.cpu().numpy().squeeze())
        history["ground_truth"].append(y_test.squeeze())


def bootstrap_ci(values, seed=77, iterations=5000):
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    samples = rng.choice(values, (iterations, len(values)), replace=True).mean(axis=1)
    return values.mean(), np.quantile(samples, 0.025), np.quantile(samples, 0.975)


for condition in conditions:
    acc = experiment_data[condition]["test_metrics"]
    loss = experiment_data[condition]["test_losses"]
    mean, lo, hi = bootstrap_ci(acc)
    print(
        f"{condition}: shortcut-free test accuracy={mean:.3f} (95% bootstrap CI {lo:.3f}, {hi:.3f}), "
        f"test loss={np.mean(loss):.3f}, correlated-val ablation accuracy="
        f'{np.mean(experiment_data[condition]["shortcut_ablation_accuracy"]):.3f}'
    )

for condition in conditions[1:]:
    differences = np.asarray(experiment_data[condition]["test_metrics"]) - np.asarray(
        experiment_data["stable_only"]["test_metrics"]
    )
    mean, lo, hi = bootstrap_ci(differences)
    print(
        f"{condition} minus stable_only test accuracy: {mean:.3f} "
        f"(95% paired bootstrap CI {lo:.3f}, {hi:.3f})"
    )

np.save(
    os.path.join(working_dir, "experiment_data.npy"), experiment_data, allow_pickle=True
)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))
for condition in conditions:
    val_loss = np.asarray(experiment_data[condition]["losses"]["val"]).reshape(10, 5)
    val_acc = np.asarray(experiment_data[condition]["metrics"]["val"]).reshape(10, 5)
    axes[0].plot(np.arange(1, 6), val_loss.mean(axis=0), marker="o", label=condition)
    axes[1].plot(np.arange(1, 6), val_acc.mean(axis=0), marker="o", label=condition)
axes[0].set(title="Validation loss", xlabel="Epoch", ylabel="BCE loss")
axes[1].set(title="Validation accuracy", xlabel="Epoch", ylabel="Accuracy")
for ax in axes:
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25)
    ax.legend()
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(working_dir, "shortcut_recovery_learning_curves.png"), dpi=160)
plt.close(fig)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
means = [np.mean(experiment_data[c]["test_metrics"]) for c in conditions]
cis = [bootstrap_ci(experiment_data[c]["test_metrics"]) for c in conditions]
errors = [[m - lo for m, lo, hi in cis], [hi - m for m, lo, hi in cis]]
ax.bar(
    conditions, means, yerr=errors, capsize=4, color=["#4c78a8", "#f58518", "#54a24b"]
)
ax.set(ylabel="Shortcut-free test accuracy", ylim=(0, 1), title="Recovery comparison")
ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(working_dir, "shortcut_recovery_test_accuracy.png"), dpi=160)
plt.close(fig)

```

function.name: submit_review
function.description: Submit a review evaluating the output of the training script.

is_bug.description: true if the output log shows that the execution failed or has some bug, otherwise false.

summary.description: if there is a bug, summarize the bug and propose a fix. Otherwise, leave it empty.

transport_note: Responses API; upstream temperature unsupported and omitted.
